Adversarial Machine Learning (AML) is a critical domain within machine learning, yet it remains under-researched. While Reinforcement Learning (RL) has seen extensive application in other areas, its potential in addressing AML challenges has largely been overlooked. This paper introduces an innovative approach to AML by leveraging RL agents, specifically utilizing the Deep Q-Learning algorithm. We propose a novel Q-Learning framework designed to learn an optimal policy for adversarial attacks, which is then used to generate effective attack strategies. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this RL-based methodology offers distinct advantages over traditional gradient-optimization techniques in the context of adversarial attacks.

This study introduces a novel algorithm designed to match astronomical sources between images captured by the Euclid and LSST surveys. The method employs a probabilistic framework that integrates both photometric and morphological data, alongside the position of objects, to facilitate the matching process. By incorporating richer photometric details, the approach achieves a 10% enhancement in matching efficiency compared to existing techniques. Furthermore, the algorithm demonstrates robustness against realistic levels of photometric errors and source contamination.

A set of cardinals is defined as nowhere stationary if its intersection with any ordinal $\alpha$ fails to form a stationary set within that specific $\alpha$. This paper establishes the existence of a set of cardinals that is nowhere stationary yet fails to be bounded. This finding resolves an issue originally raised by Shelah.

Although ontology visualization tools are abundant, they often fail to leverage the full potential of ontology graphs. OntoPlot addresses this by introducing a new visualization approach that capitalizes on the inherent structure of ontology graphs. It achieves this through a multi-level layout strategy, where the hierarchy of the graph is mirrored in a hierarchical tree structure, and a hierarchical edge bundling technique, which groups edges traversing similar paths. Furthermore, OntoPlot integrates visual encodings that represent ontological hierarchy and semantic relationships. The tool also includes a dedicated view for visualizing the ontology's meta-graph, thereby offering a comprehensive perspective on the data. Evaluations using both user studies and automated metrics demonstrate that OntoPlot enhances ontology comprehension and is particularly effective for visualizing large-scale ontologies.

This study introduces a novel approach to domain translation for speech recognition, grounded in CycleGAN. Unlike traditional methods, this approach employs CycleGAN to translate audio from one domain to another while preserving essential input features, thereby eliminating the need for paired training data. We validate this method on the ASR Cross-Domain dataset, comparing it against baseline models and existing techniques. Results indicate that our proposed method surpasses both baselines and current state-of-the-art solutions in terms of performance.

The advent of deep learning has significantly advanced generative models, enabling them to master intricate data distributions and produce realistic outputs. This progress has notably expanded the capabilities of robots tasked with perceiving and manipulating real-world objects using sensory data. While recent achievements in this domain are promising, the majority of existing methods depend on training data that is either synthetically generated or captured from static environments, thereby limiting their ability to handle the dynamic and unstructured nature of real-world scenarios. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel framework that integrates a diffusion-based generative model with an on-board LiDAR system, allowing robots to autonomously explore and learn from dynamic environments. By leveraging this approach, the system can synthesize realistic LiDAR point clouds for real-world objects and generate plausible trajectories for the robot's locomotion. We validate this method through experiments involving a physical robot navigating a warehouse setting, where the robot successfully learns from actual sensor data to create LiDAR scans and movement paths for various objects.

This study employs molecular dynamics simulations to examine the impact of molecular flexibility on the thermal diffusion factor of binary mixtures under temperature gradients. The simulations involve rigid and flexible molecules, utilizing the latter with bond vibrations modeled by harmonic oscillators. Our findings indicate that increasing molecular flexibility significantly alters the magnitude of the Soret coefficient, a change that varies depending on the specific intermolecular potential employed. Furthermore, we observe a marked increase in thermal diffusion for systems where repulsive interactions dominate, whereas systems characterized by dominant attractive potentials exhibit a reduction in this effect.

This study examines the efficacy of fine-tuning pretrained language models for automatic essay scoring. We demonstrate that models with only a few million parameters can achieve performance comparable to large-scale pretrained transformer architectures. Furthermore, we evaluate the impact of incorporating human-written scores versus simulated scores generated by other automatic systems, finding that models trained on human annotations consistently surpass those trained on simulated data. Finally, we assess the robustness of these models when trained on data from different sources, revealing that assessments derived from the same source as the test set yield superior results.

We introduce a method to convert false-positive suppression challenges into box re-ranking tasks, thereby facilitating unsupervised learning. This transformation is achieved by defining a novel criterion for the quality of candidate boxes that incorporates both the inherent attributes of each box and the spatial relationships among them. We demonstrate the utility of this approach through the creation of an unsupervised learning framework designed for candidate box re-ordering. Our method successfully identifies false positives by leveraging the interactions between objects and significantly outperforms existing unsupervised box re-ranking techniques.

This study introduces a deep learning-based method for music source separation and denoising aimed at enhancing the fidelity of poor-quality audio recordings. The approach employs a two-stage framework: first, a neural network isolates individual sound sources from a noisy mixture, and second, a denoising network refines the specific source output. The architecture of both networks is constructed using dilated convolutions and residual connections to maximize performance. The dilated convolutions allow the model to capture long-range contextual dependencies, while the residual connections facilitate gradient flow and accelerate convergence. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques in terms of performance.

This paper introduces a novel animation technique for rendering realistic throwing movements. Drawing inspiration from real-world throwing physics, the proposed method utilizes a two-stage process: first, it determines the pre-throw wind-up and the moment of release, and second, it calculates the post-release trajectory. To achieve this, the system employs a two-layered framework. The initial layer, or "thrower," governs the wind-up and release timing by utilizing a learned model trained on real throwing data. The second layer, or "thrown," simulates the object's flight path after release using a parametric model grounded in the laws of physics. We evaluated this approach across various scenarios, including different object types and diverse throwing styles. Results indicate that animations generated by our system are perceived as significantly more realistic than those produced by conventional methods.

This study investigates the impact of syntax on fluency and word reordering within Neural Machine Translation (NMT) systems. We introduce a syntax-aware attention model designed to leverage translation phrase syntax, which we evaluate alongside a baseline employing standard phrase-based alignment. Results indicate that our proposed approach significantly enhances translation fluency and substantially improves reordering accuracy.

This study introduces a new computational method designed to determine snow lines within protoplanetary discs. The approach is designed to be highly efficient, capable of generating snow line profiles for varying radial gas accretion rates and disc viscosity in a fraction of a second. The method's efficiency stems from a piecewise parabolic model of temperature profiles, which are derived by solving the heat equation and are optimized to align with specific boundary conditions. We validate the model by comparing our results against established literature, demonstrating that while the method is generally robust, it is particularly sensitive to variations in binding energies. The study concludes that while the model accurately reproduces snow lines for most volatile species, it may struggle with those possessing low binding energies.

This paper introduces a novel method for calibrating statistical models by adjusting their parameters so that the resulting parametric distribution aligns closely with the distribution derived from observed data. The approach involves minimizing a distance metric between these two distributions, utilizing a metric grounded in the concept of optimal transport. The study demonstrates that this distance metric is highly versatile, capable of encompassing various existing metrics as specific instances. Furthermore, the work presents a transport-based metric designed to assess the similarity between two datasets, which can be applied to a broad spectrum of data types.

We introduce a method to estimate the mean values of specific observables during quantum state learning, utilizing a hybrid approach that combines variational quantum circuits with classical stochastic gradient descent. The study evaluates this technique against established techniques, such as maximum-likelihood estimation, in the context of tomography for single-qubit states. The results indicate that the proposed method achieves comparable performance to these existing protocols.

We establish new asymptotic relationships for potentials with compact support within the context of geometrical optics, which in turn yield novel formulas for asymptotic expansions. These developments have been utilized to generate a new set of asymptotic expansions specifically designed for the inversion of the geometrical optics component of the Cauchy problem.

This paper introduces a novel label smoothing technique designed to enhance the robustness of machine learning models against adversarial examples. The method leverages two specific transformations: "mixture mutations," which replace an instance's class with another from the same dataset, and "transmutations," which convert a class into a new label via a transmutation map. Unlike previous approaches that rely solely on label relabeling, our method explicitly accounts for the semantic similarity between classes by utilizing these transmutation maps. We evaluate the efficacy of this smoothing approach on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating its ability to significantly boost adversarial robustness. Furthermore, our experiments reveal that the proposed method is more computationally efficient than current state-of-the-art techniques, offering a faster alternative for achieving strong robustness without sacrificing performance.

Sample-efficient methods are vital for addressing large-scale machine learning challenges, particularly when data collection is costly. Multi-task learning specifically addresses scenarios where related tasks share common features and target variables, yet existing sample-efficiency metrics often fail to account for the correlations between tasks. This paper introduces a novel sample-efficiency framework tailored to these task correlations, demonstrating that such correlations can drastically influence sample efficiency. We propose a new algorithm that leverages task relationships to achieve improved sample efficiency. Our theoretical analysis and empirical results indicate that this approach is especially beneficial in settings with a limited number of target variables.

Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success across numerous natural language tasks, yet their computational demands often hinder practical deployment. While post-training quantization (PTQ) offers a viable solution by significantly reducing model size and inference time with minimal accuracy loss, its effectiveness varies depending on the language used. This study evaluates PTQ's performance across 12 languages, contrasting it with methods like fine-tuning and Knowledge Distillation (KD). Our findings indicate that PTQ is particularly effective for low-resource languages, outperforming both fine-tuning and standard approaches. Furthermore, we observe that PTQ yields more consistent results than KD, especially in scenarios involving limited training data.

In this paper, we investigate the Tur\'an density of $r$-uniform graphs, a topic that has recently seen significant developments. Notably, Baber and Talbot recently established the asymptotic Tur\'an density for $r=5$ and proposed a conjecture for general $r$. We refute this conjecture and provide an asymptotic Tur\'an density for $r=6$. Our findings are achieved by introducing a new extremal construction method, which we believe may have broader applications.

Detecting pneumonia in chest X-rays is a critical task for public health, yet it is often hindered by the scarcity of expert-annotated data. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging image transformations to eliminate this bottleneck. By utilizing a pre-trained model trained on a large-scale dataset of natural images, we employ a learned feature extractor to generate a "style" representation. This style is then applied via transfer to chest radiographs, effectively altering their appearance while retaining diagnostic information. Our experiments demonstrate that this technique allows for a 90% reduction in the reliance on labeled data while maintaining performance comparable to models trained with full datasets. Furthermore, the method exhibits robustness across various downstream tasks, proving its utility in multiple downstream applications.

Although recent advancements in image captioning have achieved significant progress, they still depend on massive datasets for pre-training, which are often difficult to obtain. This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates prompt learning into the captioning architecture, enabling the model to generate descriptions using flexible prompt inputs. By treating prompts as a form of auxiliary knowledge, the model can effectively learn from limited data, thereby reducing reliance on large-scale pre-training datasets. Furthermore, we propose a new loss function designed to optimize both the model's internal representations and the vocabulary embeddings within the context of these prompts. Extensive experiments conducted on two standard benchmarks demonstrate that our approach surpasses current state-of-the-art methods.

Although the concept of contrastive causation has been extensively analyzed in philosophical literature, its application to the concept of harm remains underexplored. This paper argues that contrastive causation is essential for defining harm, specifically regarding the comparison of outcomes and utility. We propose a formal model that demonstrates how contrastive definitions of harm can be derived from non-contrastive ones, thereby supporting the view that both definitions are valuable. Furthermore, we show that contrastive definitions offer a more robust framework for addressing the challenges associated with the problem of negative luck.

Wildlife monitoring is a vital component of wildlife conservation, yet it faces significant hurdles due to the vast geographic areas involved and the high costs associated with manual data collection. This study introduces a novel approach to overcoming these obstacles by leveraging deep learning and computer vision for automated wildlife monitoring. The proposed system utilizes a trained deep learning model to identify and classify animals from camera trap imagery. Additionally, a data augmentation strategy was employed to enhance the model's accuracy and robustness. The research evaluates the efficacy of various image classification architectures, including ResNet, VGG, and Inception networks, to determine their optimal performance. The resulting model demonstrates strong capabilities in detecting and categorizing wildlife from trap images. Furthermore, the system's utility extends to supporting broader conservation initiatives, such as estimating population sizes and monitoring migration patterns.

Although current neural approaches for zero-shot speech translation (XSLT) have achieved notable success, they still rely on substantial amounts of unlabeled data. To address this, we introduce two complementary strategies designed to enhance XSLT performance by leveraging language models (LMs) for both data augmentation and decoding. Our first method, Zero-Shot Language Model (LSM) Pre-training, involves training a model to perform XSLT using only language model objectives on unlabelled data prior to switching to the standard translation task. Our second method, Zero-Shot Language Model (LSM) Decoding, involves generating translations via a standard model and subsequently refining them using a language model trained on unlabelled data. Notably, both techniques are versatile and can be applied to few-shot XSLT scenarios, where they yield significant performance gains.

This work examines the influence of the second law of thermodynamics on the derivation of a generalized heat conduction equation. It introduces a constitutive relation for the heat flux, characterized by a fading memory mechanism, and utilizes the energy balance equation alongside this relation to model heat propagation. By applying the Laplace transform to the resulting integro-differential equation, the authors derive an analytical solution for a one-dimensional semi-infinite solid initially at a uniform temperature, subjected to a surface heat flux. This solution is subsequently validated against known solutions for a Dirac delta function input. Furthermore, the study presents numerical results demonstrating the one-dimensional temperature evolution in a finite slab exposed to a heat flux on one side while maintaining an adiabatic condition on the opposite side.

Accurately predicting energy demand peaks is essential for grid stability, yet current forecasting methods often overlook this aspect. This study introduces a hybrid approach that integrates conventional short-term energy predictions with dedicated peak forecasts to enhance prediction accuracy during high-demand periods. By utilizing a proposed fusion method, the model synthesizes outputs from both prediction types. Experimental results using real-world data demonstrate that this strategy outperforms both standalone conventional and peak prediction models in accuracy. Furthermore, the research addresses the challenge of handling prediction uncertainty by implementing a probabilistic fusion framework. This extension enables the integration of probabilistic forecasts from both sources, with tests confirming that the probabilistic hybrid approach yields superior performance compared to deterministic fusion, as well as probabilistic-only conventional or peak models.

Recent research has shown that machine learning algorithms can be improved by incorporating knowledge. However, this approach faces a significant challenge: determining the most effective way to integrate that knowledge. This paper addresses this issue by proposing a solution based on the concept of a knowledge graph. We introduce a method for encoding information into these graphs and then utilize graph convolutional networks to generate predictions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach across various domains, including sentiment analysis, recommendation systems, and link prediction.

This paper introduces a data-driven framework designed to localize lesions in CT scans of the chest and abdomen. Unlike traditional methods, it relies exclusively on image-level labels to train a generative adversarial network (GAN) for creating synthetic lesion masks. These masks serve as initial seeds for an active contour algorithm, which refines the localization by incorporating image gradients and curvature constraints. Experimental results indicate that this approach achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods that require pixel-level annotations, while significantly reducing the labeling burden.

Although automatic vertebral identification is crucial for spine segmentation and 3D reconstruction, current techniques often rely on complex, multi-stage pipelines that are vulnerable to error propagation. This study introduces a streamlined approach to single-view vertebral labeling that surpasses existing state-of-the-art performance. The proposed method combines a novel, data-driven feature representation with a robust classifier capable of handling class imbalance. Specifically, we introduce a new feature vector that encodes both the spatial structure and local appearance of each vertebra, leveraging a learned dictionary to model the manifold structure of the feature space. For classification, we employ a discriminative nearest centroid classifier that utilizes a distance metric tailored to the learned dictionary. On the MRC+ spine dataset, this approach achieves a 96.1% mean average precision, representing a 10% improvement over the next best method and a 2.5% gain over the previous state-of-the-art.

We introduce a cavity configuration that enables the creation of long-lived, non-equilibrium polariton states, which are typically unstable due to cavity dissipation. This system relies on a single-mode optical microcavity containing a superconducting microwave resonator, where strong coupling between the two modes allows for the formation of hybrid light-matter polaritons. By applying a two-level atom as a probe to interact with these hybrid polaritons, we demonstrate that the atom's Rabi oscillations are modified by the vacuum fluctuations of the electromagnetic field within the cavity. This interaction reveals a mechanism where the probe couples to the collective excitations of the system, highlighting the role of quantum vacuum effects in stabilizing polariton dynamics. Ultimately, our findings suggest a pathway to generate and manipulate long-lived polariton states, which could have significant implications for quantum information processing and the study of many-body quantum phenomena.

Spring-based actuaries offer a compelling solution for legged locomotion by delivering high power density and efficient energy storage. However, integrating these mechanisms into compliant systems introduces complex control challenges. This paper presents a model predictive control (MPC) framework designed to address these difficulties, utilizing a full-dynamics approach that incorporates flexible transmission elements. The study validates the proposed method through simulations of a four-legged robot featuring a compliant transmission, demonstrating its efficacy in realistic scenarios.

The challenge of determining whether multi-partite quantum states are separable or entangled is a central issue in quantum information science. While current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) processors are not yet capable of executing full quantum state tomography, this study demonstrates that they can still address the complete separability problem using a hybrid approach. By combining classical computation with a minimal set of multi-partite Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) state measurements, we show that NISQ hardware can reliably detect entanglement in various multipartite configurations. Furthermore, we examine the impact of measurement errors and noise on the accuracy of these results.

The tearing mode instability is a fine-scale phenomenon that arises in the presence of a magnetic island, and its characteristics are significantly influenced by the finite gyroradius (gyro-radius) of electrons. This study examines the finite Larmor radius (FLR) effects on tearing modes within a cylindrical geometry, specifically analyzing the parity instability, the instability growth rate, and the associated electron distribution function. The analysis reveals that the electron FLR effects can suppress the parity instability, potentially eliminating it entirely. Additionally, these effects can alter the instability growth rate and the electron distribution function, potentially leading to anisotropy. The implications of these findings for the understanding of magnetic reconnection in space plasmas are discussed.

Fashion instance-level image retrieval (FIR) is a critical task for real-world applications, yet it remains challenging due to the vast fashion variety and scarce training data. Existing methods often fail to capture the essential visual attributes of fashion images, leading to suboptimal performance. To address this, we introduce a novel multi-attribute guided self-attention network (MuAGSAN) designed to enhance FIR. This approach employs a multi-attribute learning module to extract and embed key features, while a self-attention network facilitates the modeling of long-range dependencies between attributes. Furthermore, a novel loss function is proposed to optimize the feature space by emphasizing hard negative samples. Comprehensive experiments on two prominent FIR benchmarks confirm that our method surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques.

This study examines the gradient flow approach for addressing ill-posed problems, specifically focusing on the impact of selecting stopping times. We demonstrate that for a specific class of nonlinear ill-posed equations, terminating the gradient flow at an optimally chosen time yields convergence rates that match those achieved by regularized least squares. Furthermore, we establish upper bounds for the error in the gradient of the current approximation, a result that holds practical relevance for guiding the selection of stopping times.

We introduce a new cost constructor designed to resolve the issue of incorrect matching caused by occlusions during depth estimation. By utilizing a temporal consistency constraint, the proposed method effectively handles occlusions. Experimental results demonstrate that this cost constructor yields superior performance compared to existing approaches. The implementation is available at https://github.com/3D4Life/DeepCostConstructor.

The paper investigates the two-dimensional massive Thirring model, which is integrable and linked via a Manakov transformation to the Fokas-Lenells equation. We present the rational solution of the Fokas-Lenerts equation and subsequently derive a corresponding rational solution for the two-dimensional massive Thirring model. Furthermore, we examine the asymptotic behavior of this solution in both spatial and temporal limits.

We investigate embedding Fierz-Pauli and massive gravity into double field theory (DFT). By utilizing a DFT frame where the generalized metric factorizes, we demonstrate that the dynamics of both theories can be expressed through an action featuring a DFT scalar and a symmetric tensor field. This tensor field is constrained by an extension of the generalized Schouten-Nijenhuis condition. Furthermore, we derive the equations of motion for massive gravity and confirm their equivalence to standard formulations, noting that our findings hold for any choice of the generalized dilaton.

This paper introduces a channel load aware association mechanism designed to enhance throughput and minimize delay for mobile devices within Home WiFi environments. Unlike traditional RSSI-based connection methods, our approach evaluates the actual channel load of available access points. We validate the mechanism's efficacy through extensive simulations, comparing it against the widely used RSSI-based association. The results demonstrate that our channel load aware method achieves significantly higher throughput and lower delay.
